pr_comments: Code looks good BTW, just need tests for any new kernel APIs...can add them to one of the suites in tests/kernel/pipe (no I don't know why there are two of them, pick one I suppose)

**All checks are passing now.**



*Tip: The bot edits this comment instead of posting a new one, so you can check the comment's history to see earlier messages.*

> I saw that there were a few inline syscalls, so thought I might be able to get away without the verify function, but I will do it shortly.

Inline syscalls still have non-inline verification functions. If the verification functions don't exist, you get a fatal "unimplemented system call" error if you try to invoke it from user mode.

> @andrewboie - do you recommend also taking the spinlock in that case?

Oh, I didn't notice this earlier but yeah, you could get incorrect or outright goofy results if these APIs are called at just the wrong time, like if another CPU is modifying the same data...I think using the lock is safest.

> if these APIs are called at just the wrong time

We could also start with introducing these APIs as kernel-only, and wait for actual usecases for using them from userspace. The current usecase is implementing higher-level synchro primitives in kernel space (so locking would also be handled by "dependency injection" (i.e. at a higher level)). Just thinking aloud...

> > if these APIs are called at just the wrong time
> 
> We could also start with introducing these APIs as kernel-only, and wait for actual usecases for using them from userspace. The current usecase is implementing higher-level synchro primitives in kernel space (so locking would also be handled by "dependency injection" (i.e. at a higher level)). Just thinking aloud...

The potential concurrency issues we are seeing has *nothing* to do with user mode. Two supervisor threads can have the same problems.

Should be good to go now. Apologies, but the spacing is off a little in the test_pipe_avail.c comments; the 'r' and 'w' line up properly with a monospace font.

Also, I opted to remove `const` from the `pipe` parameter, because (technically speaking) `k_spinl_lock()` modifies it. It's pretty close to being a const operation though...

> The potential concurrency issues we are seeing has nothing to do with user mode. Two supervisor threads can have the same problems.

Yes, and I mean that these functions could stay kernel-only with a requirement that synchronization should be handled by the caller. I may imagine, that would work for the current usecase of https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/24813.

Of course, if we shoot straight for the userspace support of these APIs, we don't have a choice but handle locking issues right now.

issue_context.title: kernel: pipe: read_avail / write_avail syscalls
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
It's not immediately obvious how much of a k_pipe buffer is available for reading / writing (if the buffer even exists - they can be created with no buffer).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Just a few extra functions. I've already written them for buffered pipes. Handling unbuffered pipes may be a simple modification.
```
size_t k_pipe_read_avail(const struct k_pipe *pipe);
size_t k_pipe_write_avail(const struct k_pipe *pipe);
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I didn't see any other alternatives, so I just wrote them myself. 

**Additional context**
Was going to keep them static inside of my socketpair(2) implementation (#24813) but was asked to make a separate PR for this by @pfalcon CC @carlescufi .
comments: +1 for adding this functionality, the usecase is pretty clear.
